title: Rule 30 ASIC-Saturated State Machine via Binary-Tower SNARK
content:
Approved next step on the Rule 30 VDF. The shipped machine in igor-holt/rule30-vdf remains Winterfell over a 128-bit prime field: 2N columns, 4N degree-2 constraints, prime-field OR and XOR with a coefficient 2, boolean patches x^2-x. That encoding is correct only while values stay in {0,1}. It is not the native automaton.

ASIC-saturated state machine. On a periodic ring the Rule 30 step in characteristic 2 is s'_i = s_{i-1} + s_i + s_{i+1} + s_i s_{i+1}. Depth two: one AND, three XORs. Horizontal width N is parallel. Delay parameter is row count T. ASIC saturation means further silicon spend hits gate and wire delay, not an algorithmic gap. Sequentiality is the computational-irreducibility conjecture on this ring, not a theorem, and not the same system as Wolfram's single-seed half-line. Published benchmarks are CPU proof times, not ASIC cycle times.

Binary-tower verification. Diamond and Posen, Succinct Arguments over Towers of Binary Fields (ePrint 2023/1784), and the Binius / FRI-Binius stack, commit bit traces on the tower F2 subset F4 subset F16 without inflating each bit into a 128-bit field element. The AIR collapses to one degree-2 constraint per cell: y_i + s_{i-1} + s_i + s_{i+1} + s_i s_{i+1} = 0. Evaluation of T rows stays sequential. The SNARK prover may be parallel. A green proof attests the AIR and the endpoints. It does not attest irreducibility.

Out of scope for this asset: a claim that the Winterfell repository already verifies the tower AIR. It does not. src/air.rs is still F_p. Spec bind lives at docs/binary-tower-air.md.
